title: Crescendo cutover guide and observability stub - Oct 2026
content:
Purpose:
This is the working cutover guide for the 'Crescendo' release (runtime v5.2.0 + routing policy changes). Goal: minimize user-facing latency regressions, retain throughput targets, and validate new fallback behavior. This doc combines an ops checklist, short rollout calendar, and an early draft of release notes for stakeholder review.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: Release conductor, SRE on-call, serving runtime owners, product PMs, QA lead.
- Affects: Hosted API region us-west1/us-east1, Dedicated pools (beta), routing policy service.
- Out of scope: Private on-prem package (separate rollouts).

High-level timeline (UTC):
- 2026-10-18 00:00 - Pre-cutover signal window begins (telemetry baseline capture, 72h).
- 2026-10-20 02:00 - Canary push to 3% traffic (10 instances per region). 2-hour observation window.
- 2026-10-20 04:30 - Canary decision point: proceed -> 25% or rollback.
- 2026-10-20 09:00 - Gradual ramping steps every 30m: 25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 100%.
- 2026-10-20 18:00 - Post-ramp stabilization window (6h).
- 2026-10-21 02:00 - Postmortem & quick notes published (internal).

Pre-cutover checklist (owner tags):
- [SRE] Confirm canary cluster autoscaler health + headroom (INF-1874) - due 2026-10-15.
- [Runtime] Upload quantized model artifacts to artifact repository; verify checksums.
- [Infra] Reserve burst GPUs for 24h post-cutover (ticket sent to cloud-provisioning).
- [Observability] Create Dashboards: Latency P95/P99, Token-per-second, Error budget burn rate, Backend queue depth. Link: Confluence CRESCENDO-OBSERVABILITY.
- [QA] Prepare synthetic prompt set (captive test harness): 150 prompts covering short, medium, and long sequences.
- [Support] Draft canned responses for known degradations (latency, token loss).
- [Release] Dry-run the canary deployment in staging using the same rollout script.
- [Security] KMS rotation check and ensure keys accessible to new routing workers.

Cutover roles and communication channels:
- Release conductor: Sofia Ramirez (primary contact) - Slack #release-crescendo and Pager (on-call escalation).
- Canaries & metrics lead: Ethan Park - responsible for dashboards and green/red decision.
- Rollback owner: Maya Singh - initiates and validates rollback if criteria hit.
- Infra liaison: Noah Williams - capacity & burst provisioning.
- SOC contact: Priya Desai - security alert triage.

Decision criteria (Canary -> Ramp / Rollback):
Green (proceed):
- P95 latency change <= +15% relative to baseline AND P99 not increasing more than 25% absolute milliseconds.
- Error rate (5xx) does not increase above 0.2% or baseline + 50% whichever is higher.
- Async queue depth remains within 1.2x baseline.
- No new regression signals from Quality harness (prompt failure rate < 1%).

Red (rollback):
- P99 latency spike > 40% or absolute increase > 200ms for longer than 10m.
- Error rate (5xx) > 1% sustained for 5m.
- Canary instances OOM/crash loop or KV cache miss rate > 3x baseline.
- Any security incident or data-exposure alert.

Automated safety gates:
- Traffic fencing: Routing policy will auto-divert to previous stable variant if canary health probe fails 3 consecutive times.
- Quarantine: Any node-provisioning failure triggers immediate scaling halt and notifies infra liaison.

Smoke test checklist (post-deploy):
- End-to-end generation for short prompt (latency < P95 threshold).
- Streaming token continuity test (simulate network disruptions).
- KV cache warm path correctness test (cache hit rate >= 85% within 15 requests).
- Auth token expiry/refresh validation (oauth flows).
- Billing token attribution sanity checks (sample requests).

Observability stub (dashboards & alerts) - quick reference:
- Dashboard names: Crescendo - Canary Perf | Crescendo - Traffic Routing | Crescendo - Error Signals | Crescendo - Cost Delta.
- Core metrics: request_count, tokens_generated, p50/p95/p99 latency, cpu_gpu_util, kv_cache_hit_rate, request_retry_count, model_switch_rate.
- Alerts:\n  - cres-P99-spike: P99 > baseline*1.4 for 5m -> page on-call.\n  - cres-5xx-surge: 5xx_rate > 0.8% for 3m -> slack alert + ticket.\n  - cres-cache-thrash: KV miss rate increase > 200% over baseline -> infra pager.

Rollback procedures (fast and slow):
- Fast rollback: Use routing-policy abort (atomic) to reassign all traffic to previous stable variant. Validate smoke tests pass and monitor for 15m. Owner: Maya Singh.
- Slow rollback: If partial regressions observed, step traffic down using scheduled decrements (100->75->50) with 30m holds and manual checks at each step.

Post-release tasks (24-72h):
- Stabilization: Enforce 6h elevated monitoring window; SRE rotates 2h check-ins.
- Cost review: Run cost-delta job for tokens and GPU-hours; surface large anomalies.
- Quality regression sweep: QA runs extended prompt set (1k prompts) overnight and posts failures to INF-1891.
- Release notes: Finalize and publish to docs.redwood.ai/releases and send PR to engineering weekly digest.

Draft release notes (working - short):
- Feature: routing policy v2 activated for primary hosted API - improves fallback behavior when capacity constrained; introduces dynamic variant selection.
- Runtime: Serving runtime v5.2.0 - includes improved continuous batching heuristics, KV cache prefetch, and new attention kernel fallback for small sequence lengths.
- Fixes: Resolved a memory leak in the quantized transformer scorer and fixed intermittent retry loop when model variant fails priming.
- Known issues: Some edge cases where ultra-long sequences (>8k tokens) may see slightly higher p99 during first 5 minutes post-deploy while caches warm. Documentation and mitigation linked.

Open questions / risks (action items):
- Q1: Do we want to enable routing policy v2 for dedicated pools on day 0 or delay? (PM decision) - Action: Sofia to sync with Product by 2026-10-12.
- Q2: Synthetic prompt coverage may be insufficient for long-tail customer prompts. Action: QA to attach representative prompts from top enterprise 10 customers (PRIVACY review needed).
- Q3: Burst GPU quota may require cross-team approval in the cloud account. Action: Noah to escalate if not confirmed by 2026-10-14.

After-action template (postmortem quick fields):
- Summary (1-2 lines):
- Timeline (events + timestamps):
- Root cause (if any):
- Mitigation applied:
- Action items (owner + due date):
- Severity and Impact:

Quick links & references:
- Confluence: Crescendo rollout notes (CRESCENDO-OBSERVABILITY).
- Jira: INF-1874 (canary autoscaler), INF-1891 (post-release prompt regressions).
- PR: runtime pr #5123 (kernel fallback changes).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally concise; more detailed runbook pages are linked out and will be populated by observability and infra leads. Please add any missing critical checks to the pre-cutover checklist and flag any timing conflicts in this calendar.

-- end --
